milestones.title: Prenatal Vitamins
milestones.shortDescription: Daily prenatal vitamin with folic acid
milestones.details: Take a prenatal vitamin daily throughout pregnancy. Look for one with at least [400-800mcg of folic acid](https://www.cdc.gov/folic-acid/about/index.html), iron, calcium, and DHA. Folic acid is especially important in the first trimester for neural tube development.

milestones.title: First Prenatal Visit
milestones.details: Your care team will review your last menstrual period to establish your estimated due date, and will either perform or order an ultrasound for dating. [Routine initial prenatal labs](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/routine-tests-during-pregnancy) include a complete blood count, blood type and Rh(D), antibody screen, rubella immunity, syphilis, HIV, hepatitis B and C, gonorrhea, chlamydia, and urine culture. A Pap test is collected if you are due.

milestones.title: Dating Ultrasound
milestones.shortDescription: Confirm due date and check heartbeat
milestones.details: The [dating ultrasound](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/ultrasound-exams) confirms your due date by measuring your baby's crown-rump length (CRL). You'll also get to see or hear the heartbeat for the first time! This early ultrasound helps ensure accurate dating for future screenings.

milestones.title: Cell-Free DNA and Carrier Screening
milestones.details: Discuss [cell-free DNA screening](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/prenatal-genetic-screening-tests) and carrier screening with your care team. cfDNA is a screening test, not a diagnostic test. Carrier screening checks for cystic fibrosis, spinal muscular atrophy, and Fragile X, and is only needed once in your lifetime.

milestones.title: Nuchal Translucency Ultrasound
milestones.shortDescription: Ultrasound of the back of baby's neck
milestones.details: An ultrasound measuring the thickness of the back of your baby's neck, done between 11 and 14 weeks.

milestones.title: Early Diabetes Screening
milestones.shortDescription: If indicated by your risk factors
milestones.details: A hemoglobin A1c and an early 1-hour glucose tolerance test when indicated by your risk factors.

milestones.title: Maternal Serum AFP
milestones.shortDescription: Blood test screening for certain fetal conditions
milestones.details: A blood test that screens for certain fetal conditions, including open neural tube defects.

milestones.title: Detailed Anatomy Ultrasound
milestones.details: A [detailed ultrasound](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/ultrasound-exams) evaluates your baby's anatomy, growth, and placenta location.

milestones.title: 1-Hour Glucose Tolerance Test
milestones.details: Complete the 1-hour glucose tolerance test to screen for [gestational diabetes](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/gestational-diabetes). Additional testing may be recommended if the screening result is abnormal. A CBC also checks for new or worsening anemia.

milestones.title: Third-Trimester Labs
milestones.details: After 27 weeks, labs may include a complete blood count, ferritin, and syphilis and HIV screening.

milestones.title: Tdap Vaccine
milestones.details: The [Tdap vaccine](https://www.cdc.gov/vaccines/vpd/pertussis/recs/pregnant-women.html) is recommended during every pregnancy between 28 and 36 weeks. The vaccine does not cross the placenta, but your antibody response protects baby from pertussis (whooping cough).

milestones.title: Rh Immune Globulin (Rhogam)
milestones.details: For patients who are Rh-negative and not already sensitized, [Rh immune globulin](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/the-rh-factor-how-it-can-affect-your-pregnancy) is given between 28 and 32 weeks when indicated. Your blood type and antibody screen determine whether it is needed.

milestones.title: RSV Vaccine
milestones.details: Seasonal vaccination, generally September through January, given between 32 and 36 weeks. Discuss with your prenatal team if needed.

milestones.title: Flu Vaccine
milestones.details: Seasonal influenza vaccination (October through April) is recommended during pregnancy, at any trimester when available.

milestones.title: COVID-19 Vaccine
milestones.details: Discuss the current seasonal COVID-19 vaccine (fall/winter) with your prenatal team.

milestones.title: Group B Strep Test
milestones.details: A vaginal and rectal swab checks for [Group B Streptococcus](https://www.cdc.gov/group-b-strep/about/index.html). If positive, antibiotics during labor are recommended.

milestones.title: Baby's Position Ultrasound
milestones.details: Around 36 weeks, an ultrasound checks whether your baby is head-down (cephalic) or in another position.

milestones.title: Hospital Bag Ready
milestones.shortDescription: Pack your bag for the big day
milestones.details: Pack your hospital bag by 37 weeks with essentials for you, baby, and your support person. See the Hospital Bag Checklist for the full list.

milestones.title: Weekly Appointments
milestones.shortDescription: More frequent check-ups as due date nears
milestones.details: Starting around 36 weeks, you'll have [weekly appointments](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/routine-tests-during-pregnancy) to monitor you and baby closely. Your provider will check baby's position, your cervix, blood pressure, and discuss signs of labor to watch for.

milestones.title: Prepare for Delivery
milestones.shortDescription: Review your plans for the big day
milestones.details: Review your birth preferences, when to check in to Labor & Delivery, your hospital route, and any planned induction or cesarean delivery.
